Thanksgiving 2026 — where should we go?

The school break is Mon Nov 23 – Fri Nov 27. Every price is for the whole family, 2 adults + 3 kids, with everything included.

Prices checked Oct 20, 2026

At a glanceHotel mapAll trips (66)DestinationsMy shortlist
  • Prices checked October 20

    Every total is for all five of us — flights or gas, the room, taxes and resort fees, a car and bags. Flights and rooms move daily, so treat these as a snapshot and re-check before booking.

  • Kauai after Hurricane Lowell

    A Category 2 hurricane hit Kauai's south shore (Poipu) on Sept 7, 2026. Kauai is welcoming visitors again and Poipu Beach is busy, but some resorts, roads and restaurants are still being repaired, and Waimea Canyon was still closed in mid-October. The Kauai options carry a warning.

  • Mexico & Tijuana CBX travel schedule rule

    All five of us need passport books. For Cabo options using the Tijuana Cross Border Xpress (CBX), driving the Sienna to San Diego is 470 miles (~8.5–10 hours). To honor our strict rule of cutting at most ONE school day (and never on both ends), the CBX itinerary requires driving down Friday Nov 20 (cutting Friday school) and sleeping near CBX before the Saturday morning flight, then returning home on Sunday Nov 29 after a Saturday checkout. Flying home on Sunday Nov 29 is not offered via CBX because driving north on the Sunday after Thanksgiving would cut into school on Monday on both ends.

  • Maui

    Kaanapali and Kahana resorts are open; Lahaina town (just south) is still rebuilding after the 2023 fire, so we'd visit it quietly and respectfully.

Why it’s great

  • Swimmable Médano Beach right in front
  • Lowest all-inclusive price found: $7,808 for 5 nights, fully refundable
  • Two connecting rooms give the family two bathrooms
  • Earns and uses the family's RIU Class status
  • Short ride to Cabo marina for El Arco boats

Watch-outs

  • Big slides are next door, recommended for ages 12+ and 1.20 m+
  • Next-door Riu Santa Fe is a party resort (Riu Party, Pacha nightclub)
  • 35-45 minute transfer from the airport

Good to know

  • Sits on El Médano beach, which RIU calls the best spot for a swim in Los Cabos.riu.com
  • Médano is a calm bay with a sandy bottom, gradual depth and daytime lifeguards.cabo-adventures.com
  • Splash Water World is listed as a Riu Palace highlight: the slide park at next-door Riu Santa Fe. Its slides require a height of 1.20 m, and RIU recommends age 12+.riu.com
  • RiuLand kids' club for ages 4-12, with crafts, sports and games.sunwing.ca
  • Junior suites max out at 4 guests, so a family of 5 needs the Connecting Junior Suite (two rooms, max 8).sunwing.ca
  • 24-hour all-inclusive with 7 restaurants and 7 bars, and an infinity pool with Jacuzzis.riu.com
  • About 35-45 minutes from SJD airport and 4.5 km from downtown Cabo San Lucas.riu.com

Why it’s great

  • On Medano Beach, Cabo's calm swimmable bay; minutes from the marina
  • 2BR suite has full kitchen, in-unit washer/dryer and balcony grill
  • Quiet upscale pool, with slides and kids' club at sister resort next door
  • All-inclusive is optional, so the kitchen lets you cook some meals

Watch-outs

  • No water slide or kids' club on site; both are next door
  • About 35-45 minutes from SJD airport with no free shuttle
  • Medano is busy with boats and vendors; timeshare sales pitch likely

Good to know

  • Sits directly on Medano Beach, Cabo's longest calm, swimmable bay (sandy bottom, gradual depth, lifeguards and a flag system). Pacific-side beaches such as Divorce Beach have killed swimmers, but Medano is the safe one. Expect boats, vendors and crowds.cabo-adventures.com
  • The resort's own pool is a quiet, upscale two-level free-form pool with beachfront jacuzzis. There is no water slide on site.costcotravel.com
  • The Children's Club (ages 4-12, full- and half-day programs) and a family pool with a whale water slide are at neighboring sister resort Villa del Palmar, not at Villa La Estancia.costcotravel.com
  • A July 2026 local article says Villa La Estancia guests ride the slides and use the kids' club next door through sister-resort privileges. It does not say whether room-only owner-rental guests get access, so ask the owner.thecabosun.com
  • On-site dining: La Casona (breakfast buffet and dinner), La Parrilla (poolside breakfast and lunch) and Palmita Market & Deli for snacks and sodas.villalaestancia.com
  • A Feb 2026 room tour of the 2-bedroom suite shows a gourmet kitchen, in-unit washer/dryer, pantry, balcony gas grill and a second bedroom with two queens. The video says it sleeps up to 6, so confirm 8 with the owner.youtube.com
  • Airport (SJD) is about 35-45 minutes away. The resort says 45 minutes and offers paid transfers only, with no free shuttle.villalaestancia.com
  • Hotel bookings show a sanitation tax of MXN 90 (about $6) per room per night, paid at the hotel. Whether owner-rental guests pay it is not stated.costcotravel.com

Why it’s great

  • Roomy 2BR with three baths, two kings and a kitchenette; sleeps six
  • Several pools, a Kids' Club listing and on-site restaurants and mini-market
  • Quieter San Jose side, about 25-30 minutes from SJD airport
  • Calm Chileno and Santa Maria bays are a drive away

Watch-outs

  • Beach in front is rocky; reviewers say swimming there is unsafe
  • Hillside layout means lots of stairs; rooms described as dated
  • No water slide; family programming looks limited

Good to know

  • The resort has a private beach, but a Nov 2025 guest review says 'you can't swim in the ocean as there are many rocks and hence dangerous'. Treat the beach in front as a place to sit, not swim.trip.com
  • Better swim spots are a drive away: Chileno Bay (Blue Flag, lifeguards, roped-off swim area) and Santa Maria Bay are calm. Palmilla has lifeguards but is less calm. Most San Jose del Cabo beaches are dangerous for non-surfers.oyster.com
  • Raintree lists 4 pools plus a pool bar and a Kids' Club (other sites list 3 pools plus a children's pool and swim-up bar). No water slide is mentioned anywhere.raintreevacationclub.com
  • 2-bedroom units: two king beds, a pull-out sofa and three bathrooms, sleeping up to 6. The unit descriptions say 'kitchenette' while the amenity list says 'fully-equipped kitchens', so confirm the setup with the owner.raintreevacationclub.com
  • Dining on site: Inizio (Mexican/international, breakfast and dinner), Altura poolside lunch, a lobby coffee bar and room service until 11 pm, plus a mini-market.raintreevacationclub.com
  • Airport (SJD) is about 22.5 km, roughly 25-31 minutes by car. A paid airport shuttle and private taxis are available.hotels.com
  • The resort is built into a cliff. Reviewers (Oct 2025 to May 2026) describe many stairs, long walks between buildings and reliance on the resort shuttle; some rooms are called dated.trip.com
  • Hotel bookings list an administrative fee of about $18 per night plus a small city tax, and paid parking. Ask the owner whether rental guests are charged.travelocity.com

Why it’s great

  • Big-resort kid amenities: free kids club, splash pad, five pools
  • Spacious 2BR/3BA with full kitchen sleeps eight
  • All-inclusive reportedly optional for owner guests; room-only works
  • Calm Santa Maria and Chileno bays a short drive away

Watch-outs

  • Beach has rip tides and frequent black flags; no swimming
  • Adding all-inclusive costs about $588/night for five (listing rates)
  • Timeshare pitches and crowding reported; most pools are deep
  • About 35 minutes from SJD with no hotel shuttle

Good to know

  • The resort converted to an all-inclusive Marriott Bonvoy (Autograph Collection) property on July 1, 2025: 270 rooms and suites on the Sea of Cortez with eight dining venues.travelagewest.com
  • The beach in front is not for swimming. TripAdvisor reviewers (Mar and Aug 2026) cite rip tides and intense waves, and RedWeek Q&A says black-flag warnings are posted most of the time.tripadvisor.com
  • Calm swimming is a short drive up the Tourist Corridor: Santa Maria Bay (Km 13) is a protected cove with calm water, and Chileno Bay is gentle and flat, good for young children.cabo-adventures.com
  • Marriott lists a complimentary Kids Club for ages 4-12 (supervised indoor space with playground and trampoline) and 'Las Fuentes', a children's pool and splash pad. Costco's page instead says ages 4-11 and for a fee, so confirm.marriott.com
  • Five outdoor pools (one adults-only), four hot tubs and a children's pool with a mini water slide; there is no large water park or lazy river.costcotravel.com
  • Owner-listed 2BR/3BA Presidential Suite: about 1,250 sq ft, sleeps 8 (two queens plus two double sofa beds), full kitchen with stainless appliances, pots and pans.vrbo.com
  • Airport (SJD) is about 26 miles, roughly 35 minutes away. The hotel does not run an airport shuttle.marriott.com
  • Recent reviewers say nearly all pools are quite deep with few shallow areas, mention pushy timeshare presentations (about 2.5 hours), crowding from timeshare guests and confusing wristbands.tripadvisor.com

  • Airport (PVR) is about 20 minutes per the resort FAQ (Costco says about 30). There is no free shuttle; transfers cost a small fee.villalaestancia.com

Why it’s great

Good to know

  • The 2-bedroom suite has two king bedrooms, two baths and a terrace with a private plunge pool; the kitchen is partial (full-size fridge, stovetop, microwave, coffee maker). A RedWeek listing for Nov 21-28, 2026 says it sleeps 6; Vidanta's page says up to 7 adults and 3 children.redweek.com
  • Grand Bliss has its own pool with a swim-up bar. Guests may also use the Main Pool at Beachland and the Grand Mayan, Mayan Palace and Sea Garden pools. The Grand Mayan has a Lazy River (10-6:30), wave pools with the Mayan Pyramid Slide (10-6) and a kids' Aqua Park (9-9). Vidanta's page does not say Grand Bliss guests can use the lazy river or wave pools; a 2022 RedWeek review says they can.vidanta.com
  • The Mayaamigos Kid's Club and Kid's Club Aqua Park are at the Grand Mayan. A tourism-board page calls the club complimentary; eligibility for Grand Bliss guests is not confirmed.rivieranayarit.com
  • A 2024-25 review says there are no restaurants, gym or spa at Grand Bliss itself; dining is at sister resorts reached by golf cart or mini-tram, with only a lobby bar and casual poolside lunch spot on site.oyster.com
  • The Cirque du Soleil show in Nuevo Vallarta is LUDO, a water-themed dinner show that premiered Dec 12, 2025 in a 696-seat theater, with separately sold tickets and no published age guidance. JOYA is at Vidanta Riviera Maya, not here.cirquedusoleil.com
  • The BON Luxury Theme Park has a soft opening on Oct 24, 2026, exclusive to VidantaWorld guests, separately ticketed, evenings Tuesday-Saturday with limited capacity; public opening is April 2027. It does not define which guests qualify.prnewswire.com
  • The beach is on Banderas Bay; the Riviera Nayarit tourism site describes it as almost 3/4 mile wide and good for swimming (check flags daily). Airport (PVR) is about 15 minutes away.rivieranayarit.com
  • Vidanta is not all-inclusive: food and drinks cost extra unless you buy a dining package (article published 2020, updated May 2024).laurenslighthouse.com

  • Lazy river, water slide and a pirate-ship kids' pool
  • Right on North Kāʻanapali Beach, with a snorkel reef next door

Watch-outs

Good to know

  • One- and two-bedroom villas have a full kitchen, a washer and dryer, and a furnished lanai.marriott.com

  • Two heated beachfront pools with rock waterfalls and hot tubs.marriott.com
  • On North Kāʻanapali Beach. Kahekili Beach Park, with a snorkeling reef just offshore, is about 0.1 mile away. Bring fins, since rocks and reef start close to shore.hawaii-guide.com
  • Kai Ala Market in the North tower sells groceries and ready-to-eat meals, and there is a grab-and-go store in the South tower.marriott.com
  • Kahului Airport (OGG) to Kāʻanapali is about 28 miles, or 45–65 minutes outside rush hour.hawaii-guide.com
  • The 2023 fires did not reach Kāʻanapali, which is now the hub for West Maui visitors. The Lahaina Bypass leads straight there.thehawaiivacationguide.com
  • Marriott lists self-parking at $35 per night for hotel bookings, so confirm the owner's free-parking note before booking.marriott.com

The places

What each destination is like in late November.

Hawaii

Poipu (south Kauai)

Kauai's sunniest, driest resort area, and in a normal late November the south shore is the calmer side for swimming and snorkeling. In 2026 it is also the area hit hardest by Hurricane Lowell (Sept 7–8): Poipu Beach itself was busy again by early October, but Lawai Road, some oceanfront condos and a few restaurants were still being repaired, and Waimea Canyon and Kokee state parks were still closed in mid-October.

Days ~81°F, nights ~71°F · ocean ~77°F

Things to do

  • Poipu Beach Park: lifeguards, sea turtles and often monk seals (open again in Oct 2026)
  • Shave ice and shops in Old Koloa Town
  • Na Pali Coast snorkel or boat tour from Port Allen (confirm the operator is running)
  • Mahaulepu coastal walk from Shipwreck Beach (check trail conditions)
  • Spouting Horn blowhole (check access, since Lawai Road was storm-damaged)
  • Waimea Canyon: still closed after Lowell as of Oct 13, 2026, so check before planning it

Hawaii

Princeville / Hanalei (north Kauai)

Green, dramatic and quieter, with the best scenery on Kauai: Hanalei Bay, taro fields and the Na Pali cliffs. Late November is a poor month for swimming here. From mid-October to March, high surf brings strong rip currents and a pounding shorebreak, and the area gets about 7 in of rain in November, so plan beach time around calm days and lifeguarded spots. Hanalei town was open after Hurricane Lowell, and Haena State Park reopened for day hikes on Oct 15, 2026.

Days ~80°F, nights ~67°F · ocean ~76°F

Things to do

  • Hanalei town and pier: shave ice, shops, and watching the winter surf
  • Lifeguarded swims at Hanalei Bay's Pavilion or Pine Trees towers, on calm days only
  • Haena State Park day hike to Hanakapiai Beach (visitor reservation needed; reopened Oct 15, 2026)
  • Hanalei Valley lookout over the taro fields
  • Kilauea Point lighthouse and seabird refuge (check hours)
  • Na Pali Coast boat or helicopter tour (seas are often rough in winter)

Hawaii

Kailua-Kona (Big Island)

Sunny, dry and warm, with almost no rain in November. Beaches here are mostly lava rock, so families swim and snorkel at protected spots like Kahaluu Beach Park, which is calm, lifeguarded and full of sea turtles. There is a lot to do: manta ray night snorkels, historic Kailua Village, and a long day trip to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, where Kilauea has been erupting in episodes. Hurricane Lowell missed this coast; only flash flooding from its trailing moisture was reported on the Big Island.

Days ~84°F, nights ~72°F · ocean ~79°F

Things to do

  • Snorkel with sea turtles at Kahaluu Beach Park
  • Manta ray night snorkel tour from Keauhou Bay or Kailua Pier
  • Day trip to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (2–2.5 h each way; Kilauea erupts in episodes)
  • Puuhonua o Honaunau, the ancient Hawaiian 'place of refuge'
  • Historic Kailua Village and Alii Drive: Hulihee Palace, shave ice, sunset seawall
  • Kona coffee farm tour up the slope in Holualoa

Hawaii

South Maui (Kihei / Wailea)

Sunny, dry and the calmest swimming coast on Maui in late November, because winter swells mostly hit the north and west shores. Kihei is casual, with long sandy beaches and lifeguarded parks with playgrounds; Wailea next door is polished resort country with a paved oceanfront path. Calm mornings are best for snorkeling, and the first humpback whales usually show up around late November.

Days ~83°F, nights ~69°F · ocean ~78°F

Things to do

  • Snorkel boat to Molokini Crater (boats leave from Kihei and Maʻalaea)
  • Maui Ocean Center aquarium in Maʻalaea
  • Free NOAA humpback whale visitor center in Kihei (weekdays)
  • Kamaole Beach Park III: lifeguard station, lawn and playground
  • Walk the Wailea Beach Path and visit the Shops at Wailea
  • Drive up Haleakalā for sunset or a reserved sunrise

Hawaii

West Maui (Kaanapali / Kahana)

Resort-lined beaches, sunsets over Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi, and Maui's biggest family pool complexes. The August 2023 fire did not reach Kāʻanapali or Kahana, and their resorts are open; Lahaina town just to the south is still rebuilding: Front Street reopened to traffic in August 2026 and the first shop rebuild only broke ground in October, so the residential burn area remains off-limits and the town deserves a quiet, respectful visit. West-facing beaches can get winter surf, so calm mornings are best for swimming.

Days ~83°F, nights ~70°F · ocean ~79°F

Things to do

  • Snorkel the front side of Black Rock, where turtles often appear (avoid the back side)
  • Reef snorkeling at Kahekili Beach Park, north Kāʻanapali
  • Whalers Village: splash pad, playground and Hawaii Wildlife Discovery Center
  • See the penguins in the Hyatt Regency Maui lobby (free to look)
  • Old Lahaina Luau, which is running again
  • Ziplining in Kapalua, or a catamaran sail looking for early whales

Hawaii

Waikiki (Honolulu)

Hawaii's busiest beach town: a walkable strip of hotels, shops and food along a mostly gentle south-shore beach. In late November the sea is warm (about 78°F), days are in the low-to-mid 80s, and free fireworks run on Friday nights (Fri Nov 27 falls mid-trip). It is crowded, but the things kids want (surf lessons, calm walled swimming areas, the aquarium and zoo) are a short walk or ride away.

Days ~84°F, nights ~72°F · ocean ~78.5°F

Things to do

  • Beginner surf or boogie-board lessons on Waikiki's gentle Canoes break
  • Calm, walled saltwater swimming at Kuhio Beach 'The Ponds'
  • Waikiki Aquarium and Honolulu Zoo in Kapiʻolani Park
  • Diamond Head summit hike (0.8 mi; non-residents must reserve ahead)
  • Free Friday fireworks at Hilton Hawaiian Village (7:45 pm)
  • Pearl Harbor and the USS Arizona Memorial

Hawaii

Ko Olina (west Oahu)

A 642-acre master-planned resort on Oahu's leeward (west) coast, built around four rock-walled lagoons that stay calm enough for younger swimmers. The pace is slow: lagoon swims, snorkel cruises and luaus, with Waikiki 45–60 minutes away by car. Humpback whales arrive from about December, so a late-November sighting is unlikely, but sea turtles are common.

Days ~about 80–84°F, nights ~about 60–72°F · ocean ~78.5°F

Things to do

  • Swim and snorkel the four calm lagoons, linked by a 1.5-mile stroller-friendly path
  • Catamaran snorkel cruise from Ko Olina Marina (sea turtles are common)
  • Wet'n'Wild Hawaii water park in Kapolei (about 15 minutes)
  • Coral Crater Adventure Park ziplines and ATVs (about 12 minutes; most activities age 6+)
  • Luau at the resort: Marriott's Fia Fia, or Aulani's family-focused Ka Wa'a
  • Grocery run to Costco, Target or Safeway in Kapolei

Southern California

Mission Bay & Coastal San Diego

Calm bayfront beaches, waterslides and marina rentals right next to SeaWorld San Diego, with sunny late-November afternoons in the upper 60s and crisp evenings around 50°F. SeaWorld runs its Christmas Celebration daily through Thanksgiving week, and the San Diego Zoo, Balboa Park, Belmont Park roller coaster and USS Midway are all within 15 minutes.

Days ~67°F, nights ~50°F · ocean ~61°F

Things to do

  • SeaWorld San Diego Christmas Celebration (daily Nov 13, 2026 – Jan 3, 2027): coasters, dolphin/orca shows and holiday lights
  • Belmont Park & Mission Beach boardwalk: Giant Dipper wooden roller coaster, mini-golf and bike rentals
  • San Diego Zoo & Balboa Park museums (about 15 minutes away, open Thanksgiving Day)
  • USS Midway aircraft carrier museum on the downtown Embarcadero
  • La Jolla Cove sea lions and Birch Aquarium at Scripps

Southern California

Southern California Road Trips

The ultimate family road trip in your Sienna Hybrid: maximum 3 curated, high-character hotels. Explore whimsical roadside castles, Danish fairytale windmills, retro Hollywood film sets with dive-in pool movies, beachfront ice skating on Coronado Beach, and sunny desert lazy rivers.

Days ~68°F, nights ~50°F

Things to do

  • Stay in whimsical themed rooms with rock waterfall showers at the legendary Madonna Inn
  • Eat hot powdered æbleskiver in Solvang and feed towering ostriches at OstrichLand USA
  • Take the free vintage trolley from The Garland to Universal Studios Hollywood
  • Ice skate over the Pacific surf at Hotel del Coronado’s famous Skating by the Sea
  • Float the 425-foot heated lazy river and duel down 100-foot slides at Splashtopia

Southern California

Huntington Beach & Newport (Orange County coast)

Surf City is the classic SoCal beach town: a 1,850-foot pier, wide sand with beach bonfires after sunset, and Pacific City's shops and restaurants next to the hotels. The ocean is cool in late November (about 62F), so this is a beach-walk, bonfire and bike-ride trip rather than a swim trip, with Newport's Balboa Fun Zone and Balboa Island Ferry a short drive south and Disneyland roughly 30-35 minutes inland.

Days ~68°F, nights ~52°F · ocean ~62.4°F

Things to do

  • Huntington Beach Pier (1,850 ft) and Main Street
  • Beach bonfires after sunset; bike the beach path
  • Pacific City shops and dining, next to the hotels
  • Bolsa Chica Ecological Reserve: birdwatching in the largest saltwater marsh on the California coast
  • Newport's Balboa Fun Zone: Ferris wheel open daily in Nov (boardwalk rides Fri-Sun only), closed Thanksgiving Day
  • Balboa Island Ferry and whale/dolphin boats from Newport Harbor

Southern California

Dana Point & Laguna

A quieter harbor-and-bluffs stretch of coast: Dana Point Harbor has the whale-watching boats (gray whales begin passing from late November, dolphins all year), Baby Beach's calm water, and tide pools at Doheny and Salt Creek at low tide. Thanksgiving morning is the Dana Point Turkey Trot (Nov 26, with a Kids' 1-Mile Gobble Wobble), and Laguna Beach just up the coast has docent-monitored tide pools in its marine reserve.

Days ~70°F, nights ~49°F · ocean ~62.4°F

Things to do

  • Whale and dolphin watching from Dana Point Harbor (Dana Wharf tours from about $55, ~2 h; Capt. Dave's free return trip if none seen)
  • Tide pools at Doheny State Beach and Salt Creek Beach at low tide
  • Baby Beach: calm harbor water for younger swimmers
  • Ocean Institute: weekend whale and marine-life cruises and tall-ship sails (open Sat-Sun 10-3)
  • Dana Point Turkey Trot, Thanksgiving morning, with a Kids' 1-Mile Gobble Wobble
  • Laguna Beach State Marine Reserve tide pools and Heisler Park

Southern California

Anaheim (Disneyland area)

Disneyland Resort is the draw, and Holidays at the Disneyland Resort start Nov 13, 2026, so Thanksgiving week means full Christmas decor but also the year's heaviest crowds. Disney Tourist Blog lists Nov 21-27 among the worst weeks and says the Sunday-Tuesday before Thanksgiving are the busiest, with a lull late Wednesday/early Thursday; the Sunday after Thanksgiving has been uncrowded for years. It is inland and warm (highs near 77F), about 20 miles from the beach.

Days ~76.8°F, nights ~53.0°F

Things to do

  • Disneyland Park and Disney California Adventure (ticket plus park reservation required)
  • Holiday season from Nov 13: A Christmas Fantasy Parade, Haunted Mansion Holiday, Festival of Holidays, World of Color - Season of Light
  • Downtown Disney and Anaheim GardenWalk (1.3 mi from Embassy Suites)
  • Candy canes, Santa meet-and-greets (Nov 13-Dec 24) and holiday lights
  • Beach day trip to Huntington Beach (IHG lists Disneyland as 20 mi from the Kimpton)

Southern California

Greater Palm Springs (Rancho Mirage / Palm Desert)

Sunny days around the low 70s are good for the pool, but desert evenings cool off fast toward the high 40s, so a heated pool and a sweater matter. The Aerial Tramway rides about 10 minutes up to 8,516 ft, where it is often 30–40°F colder than the valley. The Living Desert's WildLights holiday lights run Nov 24, 25, 27 and 28.

Days ~72°F, nights ~49°F

Things to do

  • Palm Springs Aerial Tramway: rotating cars up to 8,516 ft, 50+ miles of trails at the top
  • The Living Desert Zoo and Gardens (8am–5pm), plus WildLights nights Nov 24, 25, 27, 28
  • Palm Springs Air Museum: walk among WWII aircraft (closed Thanksgiving Day)
  • Joshua Tree National Park day trip
  • Palm Desert Aquatic Center

Monterey, Yosemite & Tahoe

Monterey Bay & Carmel

Only 72 miles (~1 hour 15 minutes) south of San Jose, swapping airport security and I-5 traffic for Fisherman's Wharf whale-watching, the Monterey Bay Aquarium, 4-wheel surrey bikes along the coastal trail, and Point Lobos tide pools. Late November is crisp sweater weather (low 60s by day, upper 40s at night) and marks the start of monarch butterfly clustering season in Pacific Grove.

Days ~63°F, nights ~47°F · ocean ~55°F

Things to do

  • Monterey Bay Aquarium on Cannery Row (open 10am–5pm daily Nov 21–25; closed Thanksgiving Day)
  • Whale-watching tours from Old Fisherman's Wharf (humpbacks, dolphins, sea otters)
  • Rent 4-wheel surrey bikes or kayaks along the Monterey Bay Coastal Recreation Trail
  • Point Lobos State Natural Reserve & 17-Mile Drive through Pebble Beach to Carmel
  • Pacific Grove Monarch Grove Sanctuary (peak butterfly clustering begins in November)

Monterey, Yosemite & Tahoe

Yosemite & South Lake Tahoe

A 3.5-to-4-hour mountain drive from the Bay Area brings you to giant sequoias, granite cliffs, outdoor ice skating rinks, heated resort pools and early-season Sierra snow. Days are crisp (mid-40s to low 50s°F) and nights drop below freezing, so pack warm layers and carry tire chains in the trunk as required by Caltrans in November.

Days ~50°F, nights ~29°F

Things to do

  • Yosemite: walk among giant sequoias in Mariposa Grove and explore Yosemite Valley without summer crowds
  • Yosemite: outdoor ice skating at Tenaya or Curry Village, plus evening campfires and s'mores
  • Lake Tahoe: ride the Heavenly Scenic Gondola from Heavenly Village up to the 9,123-ft observation deck
  • Lake Tahoe: ice skating in Heavenly Village, snow tubing at Adventure Mountain (snow permitting), and Emerald Bay
  • Heated resort pools and hot tubs after a day in the mountains

Arizona & Sunbelt

Scottsdale & Phoenix, Arizona

One of the warmest, sunniest spots in the US in late November, with daytime highs around 74–76°F and over 85% sunshine. Direct 2-hour flights from SJC, SFO and OAK pair with sprawling desert water-park resorts and spacious 2-bedroom timeshare villas that charge zero resort or parking fees.

Days ~75°F, nights ~50°F

Things to do

  • OdySea Aquarium & Butterfly Wonderland in Scottsdale's Talking Stick district
  • Musical Instrument Museum (MIM): hands-on gallery where kids can play instruments from around the world
  • Christmas at the Princess (Fairmont Scottsdale Princess) & Phoenix ZooLights evening light displays
  • Family desert hikes at Hole in the Rock (Papago Park), Piestewa Peak and McDowell Sonoran Preserve
  • McCormick-Stillman Railroad Park (miniature trains and carousel in Scottsdale)

Arizona & Sunbelt

Sedona, Arizona

Towering red-rock buttes, canyon trails and starry desert nights about two hours north of Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. Late November brings sunny 60°F hiking days (no summer heat) and chilly evenings in the mid-30s best spent by a villa fireplace or heated whirlpool spa.

Days ~61°F, nights ~36°F

Things to do

  • Pink Jeep Tours on the bumpy Broken Arrow red-rock 4x4 trail
  • Scramble up Bell Rock Pathway, Cathedral Rock or hike to Devil's Bridge (via the free Sedona Shuttle)
  • Verde Canyon Railroad 4-hour scenic canyon train ride (35 minutes from Sedona)
  • Out of Africa Wildlife Park safari tram in Camp Verde
  • Day trip to Grand Canyon National Park's South Rim (~2 hours north)

Arizona & Sunbelt

Orlando, Florida

Warm 78°F late-November sunshine and massive family villa resorts with heated pirate-ship waterparks, waterslides and mini-golf — at a fraction of Hawaii or Mexico lodging costs. Works either as a pure resort-and-pool week or paired with theme park days at Universal, SeaWorld or Disney.

Days ~78°F, nights ~59°F

Things to do

  • On-site Shipwreck Landing pirate pool, waterslides and 9-hole mini-golf at Marriott's Harbour Lake
  • SeaWorld Orlando (5 minutes from Harbour Lake) or Universal Orlando Resort
  • Disney Springs (free admission for dining, LEGO Store and live entertainment)
  • Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (~50 minutes east on the Space Coast)
  • Airboat rides on the headwaters of the Florida Everglades at Boggy Creek

Las Vegas

Las Vegas, Nevada

Late November is sunny, dry and cool, averaging 67°F by day and 47°F at night, so outdoor pools are chilly or closed (Westgate's pool season ends Oct 25). The F1 Grand Prix takes over the center Strip on the evenings of Nov 19–21, with the race on Sat Nov 21; arriving Sun Nov 22 avoids it. The best kid days are Hoover Dam, Red Rock Canyon, family shows like Cirque's Mystère and The Wizard of Oz at Sphere, and Circus Circus' indoor Adventuredome.

Days ~67°F, nights ~47°F

Things to do

  • Hoover Dam Power Plant Tour: $15 ages 4–16, $25 adults; closed Thanksgiving Day
  • Red Rock Canyon's 13-mile Scenic Drive (timed-entry booking on Recreation.gov) and easy Red Spring Boardwalk
  • Cirque du Soleil Mystère at Treasure Island, billed as suitable for all ages
  • The Wizard of Oz at Sphere, with 4D effects
  • Blue Man Group at Luxor (recommended for ages 3 and up)
  • Adventuredome: 5-acre indoor amusement park at Circus Circus (48-inch minimum on the big rides)

Mexico & Cruises

Los Cabos

A dry desert coast with reliable sun in late November. Days are in the low-to-mid 80s, and the sea is still about 78°F. The calm, swimmable water is on the Sea of Cortez side: Médano Beach in Cabo San Lucas, plus the snorkel coves at Chileno and Santa María on the corridor. The Pacific side and most of the San José del Cabo hotel beach are for looking at, not swimming. Kids will like the boat ride to El Arco, snorkeling in the protected coves, and the resort water parks.

Days ~84°F, nights ~66°F · ocean ~78°F

Things to do

  • Glass-bottom boat from Cabo marina to El Arco and Lover's Beach
  • Snorkel the calm, protected coves at Chileno Bay or Santa María Bay
  • Swim and paddle at Médano Beach, the town's calm, lifeguarded bay
  • Wander San José del Cabo's old town and Plaza Mijares
  • Farm-to-table lunch at Flora Farms near San José del Cabo
  • Sunset catamaran cruise past Land's End

Mexico & Cruises

Mexican Riviera & Baja Cruises (from LA / Long Beach)

Drive the Sienna to Long Beach or San Pedro (or take a 75-minute Southwest hop to LGB), board the ship once, and get staterooms, all meals, waterslides, kids/tween clubs and nightly shows included. Longer 6- and 7-night sailings reach warm 85°F Cabo San Lucas and Puerto Vallarta without paying $9,000+ for holiday flights to Mexico.

Days ~84°F, nights ~68°F · ocean ~79°F

Things to do

  • Onboard waterparks, twisting waterslides, ropes courses, mini-golf and (on Norwegian Encore) at-sea Go-Karts and laser tag
  • Cabo San Lucas port days: glass-bottom boat to El Arco, Medano Beach swimming and camel/ATV excursions
  • Puerto Vallarta & Mazatlán port days (7-night Encore): Malecón boardwalk, zip-lining and beach clubs
  • Catalina Island & Ensenada port days (4-night Firenze): Avalon golf-cart tour and La Bufadora blowhole
  • Complimentary youth and tween clubs (Camp Ocean / Circle C for ages 12–14 / Splash Academy) plus full Thanksgiving dinner at sea

Mexico & Cruises

Puerto Vallarta

A real Mexican town on Banderas Bay: a seaside Malecon boardwalk, a cobblestone old town and jungle coves to the south. Late November is hot, dry and sunny, the bay is warm (about 82-84F) and usually calm, and the airport is inside the city, so hotel-zone resorts are 10-15 minutes away.

Days ~86°F, nights ~69°F · ocean ~82°F

Things to do

  • Malecon boardwalk: street performers, sculptures, sunset walks
  • Boat or snorkel trip to Los Arcos rocks, off Mismaloya cove
  • Las Caletas beach & adventure park by boat (kids' zip line, lemurs)
  • Vallarta Botanical Garden, about 15 minutes by bus beyond Mismaloya
  • Zip-line canopy tours (minimum age 8)
  • Whale season starts in December, so expect few or no whales in November

Mexico & Cruises

Nuevo Vallarta (Riviera Nayarit)

A planned resort strip across the state line in Nayarit, about 15-22 minutes north of the airport, with more than 5 miles of beach and a big marina. Its long golden-sand beaches with gentle waves are among the bay's calmest for kids, but it is resort-bound: downtown Puerto Vallarta means a taxi ride.

Days ~86°F, nights ~69°F · ocean ~82°F

Things to do

  • Long beach walks and sandcastles on the calm bay beach
  • Boat to the Marietas Islands, about 15 min from Punta de Mita
  • Sea turtles nest on the local beaches in winter
  • Stroll the Nuevo Vallarta / Paradise Village marina
  • Taxi or Uber into Puerto Vallarta for the Malecon boardwalk

Portland & Pacific Northwest

Portland, Oregon

Pacific Northwest autumn magic: Powell’s City of Books (the world’s largest bookstore, an entire city block), OMSI with real submarine tours, the 1.5-million-light Oregon Zoo ZooLights, roaring waterfalls along the Columbia River Gorge, and world-class food cart pods.

Days ~52°F, nights ~40°F

Things to do

  • Browse color-coded rooms at Powell’s City of Books in the Pearl District
  • Wander through Oregon Zoo ZooLights (1.5M twinkling lights & animal lanterns)
  • Tour the USS Blueback submarine and hands-on labs at OMSI
  • See thunderous Multnomah Falls cascading in the Columbia River Gorge
  • Feast on wood-fired pizza and artisan frites at the Cartopia & Hawthorne food cart pods

How we priced this

  • Every total is for all five of us: getting there (flights for 5, or gas for the Sienna), the room or villa with taxes and resort fees, a rental car or airport transfers, parking, and 3 checked bags. Food and activities are not included — except on cruises and at all-inclusive resorts.
  • Flights: the cheapest nonstop round trip for 5 from SJC, SFO or OAK, checked on Kayak (and Southwest on southwest.com) on Oct 20, 2026. Some of the cheapest Hawaii fares come home on a red-eye. Fares change daily.
  • Bags: 3 checked bags at $45 each way (2026 fees on Southwest, Alaska, Hawaiian and United).
  • Hawaii hotels: nightly rates from the original research, plus Hawaii's 18.712% hotel tax and resort charges and parking as listed on the hotels' own sites.
  • Timeshare weeks: the RedWeek listing total (includes RedWeek's booking fee) plus the taxes, resort fees, parking and meal plans each listing says are paid at the resort. These rentals are usually non-refundable once confirmed.
  • Resort hotels (SoCal, Monterey, Yosemite, Phoenix/Scottsdale, Sedona): live suite, 2-bedroom casita/cabin, or two-room prices with tax for Sat Nov 21 – Thu Nov 26, plus resort fee and parking.
  • Cruises from Long Beach / Los Angeles: total cruise fare for 5 guests (two connecting/adjacent staterooms) including port taxes, mandatory daily crew gratuities ($16–$20/person/day), and either driving to the port with terminal garage parking ($22–$23/night) or flying to Long Beach (LGB) with Uber XL transfers. All shipboard meals and entertainment are included.
  • Mexico & CBX Cross-Border Express: priced for all five guests in one booking, plus private SUV airport transfers. Cabo timeshares also include a "Via CBX (Cuts Fri Nov 20 only)" option: driving to the Otay Mesa CBX terminal in San Diego, walking across the enclosed skybridge into Tijuana Airport (TIJ), and flying nonstop to Los Cabos (SJD). Because driving San Jose ↔ San Diego is 470 miles (~8.5–10 hours), this option requires driving down Friday Nov 20 (cutting 1 school day) and sleeping near CBX, while strictly protecting Sunday Nov 29 for the drive home so Monday school is never missed (honoring the rule: maximum 1 school day cut, and never on both ends).
  • Rental cars: live Kayak prices for the cheapest minivan or full-size SUV that fits five plus luggage.
  • Driving: gas at $6.10/gal (California average, week of Oct 12, 2026) and 35 mpg in the Sienna Hybrid, plus 150 miles of local driving.
  • Every option leaves on a Saturday, Sunday or Monday of Thanksgiving break and is home by Sunday Nov 29, so no school is missed.
